subject: Quantitative Aptitude
topic: Mensuration 2D — Areas, Perimeters, and Diagonals (Set W9)

questions.stem: Find the area of a rectangle with length 12 cm and breadth 8 cm.
questions.explanation: B is correct. Area = length × breadth = 12 × 8 = 96 cm². Perimeter = 2(l+b) = 2(12+8) = 40 cm (distractor C). Option A (80) comes from 10×8.

questions.stem: The radius of a circle is 7 cm. What is its area? (Use π = 22/7)
questions.explanation: C is correct. Area = πr² = (22/7) × 7² = (22/7) × 49 = 22 × 7 = 154 cm². Distractor A (44) = circumference. Distractor D (308) = 2 × area. Short Trick: For r=7, area is always 154 cm² — memorise this benchmark.

questions.stem: Find the area of a triangle with base 10 cm and height 6 cm.
questions.explanation: B is correct. Area of triangle = ½ × base × height = ½ × 10 × 6 = 30 cm². Distractor A (60) is the product without the ½ factor — the most common error. Distractor C (16) = base + height.

questions.stem: Find the area of a trapezium with parallel sides 10 cm and 6 cm, and height 4 cm.
questions.explanation: C is correct. Area of trapezium = ½ × (sum of parallel sides) × height = ½ × (10+6) × 4 = ½ × 16 × 4 = 32 cm². Distractor A (24) uses only the smaller side. Distractor B (40) = 10×4. Distractor D (64) = (10+6)×4 without the ½.

questions.stem: A rhombus has diagonals of length 12 cm and 16 cm. What is its area?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Area of rhombus = ½ × d₁ × d₂ = ½ × 12 × 16 = 96 cm². Distractor A (192) omits the ½. The side of this rhombus = √(6²+8²) = √100 = 10 cm (half-diagonals form a 6-8-10 right triangle). Short Trick: d₁ × d₂ ÷ 2.

questions.stem: The diagonal of a square is 10√2 cm. What is the area of the square?
questions.explanation: C is correct. For a square of side s: diagonal = s√2. So s√2 = 10√2 → s = 10 cm. Area = s² = 100 cm². Short Trick: Area = (diagonal²)/2 = (10√2)²/2 = 200/2 = 100 cm².

questions.stem: The circumference of a circle is 44 cm. Find its area. (Use π = 22/7)
questions.explanation: C is correct. Circumference = 2πr = 44 → r = 44/(2 × 22/7) = 44 × 7/44 = 7 cm. Area = πr² = (22/7) × 49 = 154 cm². Key: first find radius from circumference, then compute area.

questions.stem: A rectangle has perimeter 50 cm and its length-to-breadth ratio is 3:2. Find its area.
questions.explanation: C is correct. Let l = 3k, b = 2k. Perimeter = 2(l+b) = 2(3k+2k) = 10k = 50 → k = 5. So l = 15 cm, b = 10 cm. Area = 15 × 10 = 150 cm². Short Trick: Half-perimeter = l+b = 25; ratio 3:2 splits 25 into 15 and 10.

questions.stem: Find the area of an equilateral triangle with side 6 cm.
questions.explanation: B is correct. Area of equilateral triangle = (√3/4) × side² = (√3/4) × 36 = 9√3 cm². Distractor C (18√3) = (√3/2)×36, forgetting the division by 2. Short Trick: Formula = (√3/4)s². For s=6: 36×√3/4 = 9√3.

questions.stem: A sector of a circle has radius 14 cm and central angle 90°. Find the area of the sector. (Use π = 22/7)
questions.explanation: A is correct. Area of sector = (θ/360°) × πr² = (90/360) × (22/7) × 14² = (1/4) × (22/7) × 196 = (1/4) × 616 = 154 cm². Arc length = (90/360) × 2 × (22/7) × 14 = 22 cm. Distractor B = full semicircle; D = full circle area.
